definitions.probe_reliability: a run counts when it produced an artifact, the sandbox was removed, every port it used is closed, the boot stayed inside the budget (real runs only — see R19 below), and the run stated a conclusion (unknown included: refusing to judge an unsettled tree is an answer)
definitions.real_pass_rate: go / (go + blocked) over real runs; unknown is listed separately and never folded into either side
definitions.failure_shape: conclusion + reason messageId (+ the row phase when the reason names one)
definitions.boot_budget: the 20s boot budget gates REAL candidates only. A fixture built to never settle costs boot + the 15s settle timeout ≈ 21s by construction, so counting it would fail the gate for a reason that says nothing about a candidate. Fixture timings are published below and never hidden (R19, HUMAN-signed)

wall_clock.source: steps[boot].ms — the whole step, including the settle wait and the kill wait
wall_clock.note: measured (T-314): a judged candidate is dominated by the sample wait plus render + kill + post-kill; a tree that never settles no longer pays a replacement window — ADR-0008 E removed it for settled:false samples (that window alone was ≈20s in R23), so what is left is the hook settle plus the same render/kill tail

boot_breakdown.note: sampleWaitMs is the sample wait only; since ADR-0008 E the replacement window is opened for an {error} sample alone, so a settled:false reading converges immediately (the artifacts record inventory.replacement_waited instead of leaving it to be inferred)

checks.detail: 12/12 real sampled run(s) within 20000ms · 1 fixture(s) over budget by construction (fixture-slow-overrun=21300ms)

limits: real plugins are a convenience sample picked by hand from npm search, not a random sample of the ecosystem
the pass rate says "this batch of pinned plugins composes on this sandbox runtime", not "plugins work"
synthetic and fixture failures are labelled and excluded from the pass rate; they only count as shapes
